dialogues.speaker: Edler
dialogues.text: #Oh, if it isn't the Proto-Boss, {NICKNAME}! Miss Yelan said you'd be joining us for this operation...

dialogues.speaker: Edler
dialogues.text: Everything's in place and absolutely airtight — that "Dark Financier" and his last few minions might as well clean their necks and get ready to meet Madame Guillotine.

choices.text: You're back already? That was quick!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: All I have to do is help Miss Yelan distract a couple of bad guys. It's easy work and there are no tight deadlines to deal with.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Corder and Doddamani are tailing me pretty tightly. I spent a good few hours eating sweet treats with Hautemontagne and they had to stand there the whole time, pretending to be tourists perusing the tea!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: I gave Hautemontagne a heads-up beforehand and told her to let the shopkeeper know to add a couple of zeroes to all the prices as a special offer for our hapless friends.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: In the end, they had to buy something, otherwise they'd have looked too suspicious. It was a real struggle for Hautemontagne and I to keep straight faces!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: It's a good way to help out the folks in Qiaoying Village by giving them a little extra income. Plus, I feel like I'm making amends for leading those criminals into their peaceful little hamlet.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: I can't help feeling like I've brought them bad fortune. Maybe milking that bad fortune for money will replace it with an auspicious air?

choices.text: You're starting to sound more and more like a Liyue local...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Hehe, you can chalk that up to me doing my homework — and my incredible talent for tongues!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Back when we were fourth-grade deskmates, Hautemontagne used to say my impressions of our teacher were spot on! It's a skill that's been remarkably useful for my work...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: "When it comes to being a detective, it pays to be a cultural chameleon. Talk cute when chatting to kids, speak cultured when conversing with the Liyue elite..."

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: "And if you happen to find yourself rubbing shoulders with criminals, make sure you know how to swear like a sailor."

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: That's what Captain Grosrochard told me.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Though now that I think about it, I can't recall ever hearing him swear. Maybe when we're taking this lot in, I might get the chance to witness his sea legs at work. Or sea mouth, rather.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: I'm looking forward to it!

choices.text: There's something familiar about your current way of speaking...
I'm not sure getting so excited over swearing is entirely healthy...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Don't worry, I won't be going around slinging profanities in front of any children. Whenever there are kids around, I talk like I'm reading a whimsical fairytale. And I certainly wouldn't say anything untoward when performing my official duties!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: You've gotta put on a menacing show when dealing with the worst of the worst. Otherwise, you'll soon find that they're the ones dealing with you!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: It's no skin off my back if criminals start calling me "executioner" or "guillotine." Though scary-sounding names like that are probably best left for heavy hitters like you.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Why don't you try throwing a few fierce words about?

choices.text: I—I guess I could try being a little more intimidating?

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: That's the spirit! Give 'em the ol' vocal evisceration!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: With your power and prestige, you wouldn't even need to be all that mean to leave the bad guys trembling.

choices.text: I need to be polite, or else I might lead Paimon astray...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: *sigh* Fair point. All of my colleagues keep saying how smart and sweet your little companion is. It wouldn't be right to be a bad influence on her.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: In which case... you can be fierce in secret, when Paimon isn't looking or listening!

choices.text: "Last few minions"?

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Indeed. This operation's been going on for months now, and Miss Yelan's actions have been quick and decisive. I've never seen someone work with such efficiency!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Right now, only the Dark Financier's closest confidants remain free, and his operations have been scaled back immensely. It's only a matter of time before he's caught in our net...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: You don't think we're catching too few criminals to be worth your time, do you?

choices.text: Not at all. One big fish is worth a hundred tiny minnows.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: That's great to hear! If you want to help out in the future, I'll make sure to pick only the most difficult cases for you to crack. The hard ones are always the most fun!

choices.text: Well, a little. I do have a quota to fulfill.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: I'm sorry to hear that! If you want to help out in the future, I'll make sure to let you know as early as possible. That way, there'll be more low-level grunts for you to round up!

choices.text: Actually, I'd like to learn more about these perps we're after.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: You're looking for the lowdown on the Dark Financier's gang? What exactly do you want to know?

choices.text: About the Mora-laundering scheme...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Of course. I'm sure Miss Yelan's already explained the basic hustle to you — they purchase items at auction with artificially inflated valuations and then, after enough such trades, the dirty Mora becomes impossible to trace.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Besides just exploiting the auction rules that allow buyers and sellers to remain anonymous, they have a whole bunch of other tricks to cover their tracks.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: For example, the Mora used to buy foreign valuables changes hands many times beforehand, even being used to buy other goods, which are then traded back for Mora elsewhere. They do this to escape surveillance.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Then, when they buy things abroad, they either use false personas or pay other people to make the purchases for them, which makes them virtually impossible to track through the stores' ledgers.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: On top of that, the "valuables" they sell at auction are actually just regular items. The sort of thing that's difficult to identify and track and then intercept in transit. Even if we do hunt one down, it usually doesn't help our case against the gang.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Just thinking about it is enough to make you want to scream, am I right?

choices.text: Yeah... I can feel my blood beginning to boil!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: And the Dark Financier has other ways of laundering money. Fake charitable foundations, film investments, shell corporations, the list goes on...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: He's been aggressively swallowing up the competition and acquiring their tricks and techniques in the process.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: But right now, things are in our favor.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Thanks to the help of the Spina di Rosula, we've managed to dismantle his network of dirty tricks and put a stop to most of his operations in Fontaine.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: As for this racket with the auction houses, it's already largely under our control — we've left a few loopholes open, but only so we can monitor who's using them.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: With your help, it's only a matter of time until we strike a decisive blow and take out the Dark Financier once and for all!

choices.text: Only a little. I'd like to give them a standard-issue beating.
How will you deal with the criminals?

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: I'm glad you asked!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: This matter concerns both Fontaine and Liyue. Besides the Dark Financier and his multiple layers of underlings, there are many people who have been unwittingly sucked into these crimes.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Following discussions between both nations, the current agreed-upon plan is for Liyue to round up and process all of the criminals within its territory, interview the suspects, and take statements in preparation for building a case.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: After which, Fontaine will arrange for the extradition of all related Fontainian subjects, whose assets will be thoroughly investigated to make sure that no guilty parties escape justice.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Once the Dark Financier is in custody, both nations will reconvene discussions to establish a joint body to prosecute all the criminals that have been caught.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Based on my experience, I imagine anyone who was paid to buy goods is going to have to forfeit whatever money they made and undergo some sort of correctional course — provided they didn't know they were aiding and abetting a criminal organization, that is...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: For members of the organization themselves, those at the third-tier and above are facing a minimum of ten years behind bars.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Whereas the Dark Financier himself can expect to live out the rest of his days in a jail cell.

choices.text: Let's make sure we solve this case!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: That's the spirit! I look forward to watching you work.

dialogues.speaker: Roxane
dialogues.text: Are the bad guys all here, Colonel Lin?

dialogues.speaker: Sergeant Lin
dialogues.text: Indeed. This is the final group of criminals to undergo interrogation. We've taken their statements. Now they're ready to join the other five groups on the ship.

dialogues.speaker: Roxane
dialogues.text: There's more of them than I expected... The worst lowlifes that Fontaine has to offer. We'll make sure they learn their lesson. By the time we're through with them, they won't dare do anything to disgrace the nation ever again.

dialogues.speaker: Roxane
dialogues.text: We appreciate your help, Colonel Lin!

dialogues.speaker: Roxane
dialogues.text: If you ever find yourself in Fontaine, I'll be sure to treat you to lunch at the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol's Melusine cafeteria. The buttered Tidalga is to die for!

dialogues.speaker: Sergeant Lin
dialogues.text: My sincerest thanks for the offer. Though my duties are set to keep me in Chenyu Vale for a good ten years, I hope that one day I can take you up on it.

dialogues.speaker: Roxane
dialogues.text: Ten years? That's hardly any time at all...

dialogues.speaker: Sergeant Lin
dialogues.text: Also, it really would be remiss of me not to mention that I am, in fact, a sergeant. Our system of ranks and responsibilities in the Millelith is quite different from those of the Maison Gardiennage and the Fontainian Navy of old.

dialogues.speaker: Roxane
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I quite understand. You Millelith are a modest bunch with a simple set of ranks. Nothing too fancy on the taxpayers' dime...

dialogues.speaker: Roxane
dialogues.text: But in my eyes, your responsibilities are worthy of the rank of colonel, and so that's what I plan to call you. Unless you deem it inappropriate, in which case I can call you sergeant after all.

dialogues.speaker: Roxane
dialogues.text: I hope one day we can establish a joint force — after all, it's been a pleasure working with you. We made light work of this little issue, I can only imagine what it would be like for our troops to unite against a horde of monsters!

dialogues.speaker: Sergeant Lin
dialogues.text: I'm sure you'd have achieved the same results without us, given a bit more time to get to grips with the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Corder
dialogues.text: Please, officer, these goods need to be processed before the auction. If you could see your way to letting me deliver them...

dialogues.speaker: Fonck
dialogues.text: My apologies, Mr. Corder, but the Maison Gardiennage suspects that your goods have caught the attention of a criminal organization.

dialogues.speaker: Fonck
dialogues.text: Both you and your goods must remain under the protection of the Maison Gardiennage until the auction starts. Otherwise, who knows what might happen?

dialogues.speaker: Corder
dialogues.text: B—But... there's still so much to do before the auction...

dialogues.speaker: Fonck
dialogues.text: Do I have to explain the meaning of the word "must" to you, Mr. Corder?

dialogues.speaker: Corder
dialogues.text: N—No... I understand...

dialogues.speaker: Doddamani
dialogues.text: I—I'd best be getting back to the ship... G—Good luck, Corder...

dialogues.speaker: Fonck
dialogues.text: Please wait here just a moment, Mr. Doddamani. The safety inspectors haven't finished checking your ship yet. Once it's done, you'll be free to return to Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Doddamani
dialogues.text: O—Okay...

dialogues.speaker: Friendly Passenger
dialogues.text: Is there something wrong with the ship? Why is the Maison Gardiennage here...?

dialogues.speaker: Crewmember
dialogues.text: #Ah... Haha... I'm sure it's nothing. I think I saw the famous adventurer, {NICKNAME}, helping out, which means everything's certain to be under control.

dialogues.speaker: Crewmember
dialogues.text: No matter the situation, the captain can surely sort it out...

dialogues.speaker: Crewmember
dialogues.text: I just did what I was told... I won't get into trouble, right...?

dialogues.speaker: Keshen
dialogues.text: I heard you were a fighter — the famous Treasure Hoarder, Scamface!

dialogues.speaker: Keshen
dialogues.text: I've heard your vile title more times than I can count over the past ten years. We've been looking forward to meeting you. It's just a pity you're always on the run.

dialogues.speaker: Keshen
dialogues.text: According to our intel, your patron, the Dark Financier, studied under the same master as a certain Rocky Avildsen... So, he decided to take you on, and you're not even his equal?

dialogues.speaker: Keshen
dialogues.text: How about we go another round or two? I'll even up the odds and fight you one-handed! But after that, we're taking you in.

dialogues.speaker: Scamface
dialogues.text: Tch... I can't fight any more than I can run. You broke my leg with that kick.

dialogues.speaker: Scamface
dialogues.text: How did you do it? I led you into a minefield, and you just ran on through without a scratch!

dialogues.speaker: Scamface
dialogues.text: And you! I saw you take the full force of two of my explosives... and what, you're barely even grazed? Even a clockwork meka couldn't shrug that off...

dialogues.speaker: Keshen
dialogues.text: You call that a minefield? Xuanzhu's overhead surveillance device and metal detector made short work of your paltry traps.

dialogues.speaker: Keshen
dialogues.text: And your explosives leave a lot to be desired — I've taken worse hits from a Xuanwen Beast.

dialogues.speaker: Scamface
dialogues.text: If I'd known things would turn out like this, I wouldn't have taken the Dark Financier's Mora and come back to Liyue...

dialogues.speaker: Keshen
dialogues.text: You can mull over your mistakes in prison, once you've got down on your knees and groveled for forgiveness from that ship full of passengers.

dialogues.speaker: Xuanzhu
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}! I didn't think you'd have much time for keeping the peace out here, what with helping to crack the case...

dialogues.speaker: Xuanzhu
dialogues.text: We've already apprehended the criminal, so there's no need for you to get your hands dirty!

choices.text: Good job!

response.speaker: Xuanzhu
response.text: We're just fulfilling our duty!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "Scamface" finally buckles under terror and remorse... not daring to utter another word.

choices.text: Make sure to teach him a lesson!

dialogues.speaker: Fonck
dialogues.text: What's wrong? Legs shaking from fear?

dialogues.speaker: Fonck
dialogues.text: You didn't seem all that scared when you were out there making your dirty money.

dialogues.speaker: Fonck
dialogues.text: You didn't stop to think about all the people your money laundering was hurting, did you? Now, you've suddenly woken up and realized you'll have to face the ire of the people. Is that it?

dialogues.speaker: Fonck
dialogues.text: When it comes time to face the music, it turns out you're nothing more than a simple coward...

dialogues.speaker: Corder
dialogues.text: I'm ready to face my judgment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And I'm ready to be in the audience, pelting you with tomatoes.

dialogues.speaker: Corder
dialogues.text: You...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Or would you prefer rotten eggs?

dialogues.speaker: Corder
dialogues.text: It must be fate that I've ended up in your hands.

dialogues.speaker: Fonck
dialogues.text: Haha! Throw one for my sake, won't you?

dialogues.speaker: Fonck
dialogues.text: Oh, and there's also my colleague, Consigliere's Ex-Left Hand. He has other matters to attend to, so he can't be at the trial. It would be great if you could hurl a... rotten apple in his stead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe, {NICKNAME}, Paimon's back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Officer Edler took Paimon along to question those meany-weany bad guys. Paimon learned a lot about interrogations!

choices.text: So you had fun?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So much fun! Making bad guys break down and admit their motives, and then be all like "I'm so sorry, I regret everything." It's like putting a big fat period at the end of a horrible sentence!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about you? Did Yelan enjoy her holiday?

choices.text: We had a great time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon didn't realize before, but thinking about it, Yelan really is an expert at being busy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Catching all these oh-so-many criminals and making it look like a piece of cake...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* The next time we see her, Paimon'll have to ask how she does it. Maybe she can teach Paimon how to manage her time better and still stay full of energy!

choices.text: Why are you so motivated all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon just wants to help you as much as she can!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You keep getting stronger, so Paimon has to work hard to keep up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, it's time for our next adventure. Let's go!

choices.text: Paimon, the eager student. I'm impressed!
We agreed to meet up in Nod-Krai.
Did you intimidate any bad guys?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon hopes so...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's forehead hurts from pulling mean faces, and Paimon's eyes hurt from giving scary stares.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #As soon as they heard Paimon's companion is the great and mighty {NICKNAME}, the bad guys almost wet themselves! They told us everything we wanted to know after that.

choices.text: Maybe I should try being a little more intimidating...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Paimon's trying really hard, but Paimon just can't picture it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME} is always so nice and calm. You never get angry when you talk to Paimon. Even at your fiercest, being scary's not your thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You don't get mad when facing ordinary bad guys. So, what would it take to make you really lose your temper? A super-duper bad guy? A super-duper-wuper bad guy?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've been through a lot — too much to get our feathers ruffled by run-of-the-mill scoundrels!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're right. We're above all that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: With everything we've seen this time, we're sure to take future adventures in our stride!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No matter what we face, Paimon hopes that {NICKNAME} can always stay calm and come out on top!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That way, Paimon doesn't have to worry, and we can carry on being super happy once the bad guys are dealt with!

choices.text: ...Like turning myself into an avatar of pure terror...
...And leaving the bad guys running away, screaming and crying...
